editorial:
Imagine moving into your first real home with your partner, only to realize you aren't actually alone. You follow Micah and Katie as they settle into a quiet suburban house that feels totally normal at first. The vibe is very grounded because the whole story is told through their own home security cameras and handheld video. It starts with tiny things, like a door closing on its own or a weird noise in the kitchen, but it quickly turns into something much scarier. You will feel like you are spying on a real couple as they try to figure out if their house is actually haunted by something evil.

What makes this work is the slow build. It doesn't rely on big monsters, but rather the fear of what you can't see. While the slow start might bore some people, the tension pays off in a huge way. It is a great pick if you love movies that make you look twice at your own bedroom door before you turn off the lights.
endingExplained: At the end, Katie becomes fully possessed by the demon. She attacks Micah and kills him in their bedroom. The camera captures the scary moment she drags his body away. Then, she turns the camera on herself and gives a creepy smile. The movie ends with her attacking the person filming, leaving you to realize that the entity has completely taken over her body and won the battle.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves found-footage films and psychological scares.
